meeting.title: Interview L2 :  Mohan Krishna Palakurti for Project Manager role | Saturday Oct 24, 2026 @ 7.30 - 8 pm (IST)

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Hey, hi, hey, I go, hey...

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: So Kailash is one of the co-founders, so we wanted to have this discussion with him too. So Kailash, I had a discussion with Mohan last time. I want you to start and then I will take over.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Okay, sure. So, again, nice to meet you, Kailash. I look over the sales Dataskate. So, I would like to know more about you and kind of catch up with a couple of questions as you brought us.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So let me introduce myself. I'm Hon. Krishna Balakulti be of Hyduba. My recent companies call in aerospace wherein they are into the aerospace domain and they have products like flight management system, seating structure, and evacuation systems and all those things.
Those will be deployed across all the Boeing and other company flights. So here I'm working as a cure manager, even though the designation as a cureer manager, my roles and responsibilities are more into the project management and project delivery. Looking into the project deliverables.
So here I'll be involved before the idea comes into the picture wherein, for example, if any idea comes and if we want to progress that into the implementation and delivery, then we will step in there. We'll see how the value is generated based on the idea, what to do and what not to do, and how much budget is required, how many resources are required, and all those things and what kind of tools are required here. All those things we will analyze and based on the ROI and the business use case, we will get the BU approval here, and once we get the approval, then we'll start with the resourcing and implementation phases there.
Once we complete the implementation with dev QA and all, we'll have multiple stages like dev QA, pre-production phases, and once everything goes fine, then we'll deploy that into the production environments and we'll make sure that all the users are compatible with that application here.
If we see any issues, then we will have the maintenance fees as well like production if we get any production. Berks if we will be handling those and... On a higher level, I'm involved in the end-to-end process of a project life cycle, including all the various minute things as well like budgeting, resourcing, and infrastructure-related
tools. What tools we have to use and what technology we have to use, and whether the in-house is useful or how we can hire them. Whether it can be a contractor or a full-time based on the project size. I have a team of 22 people wherein I deal with around 20-5 projects here. Concogent projects and the project size start from two months to two years projects.
Wherein all these projects are with the web API, SAP, and mobile applications. All these are...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
So now it's good that you're handling different streams of projects. I'm sure that majority will not have knowledge of streams to understand the projects and do it. So how is your approach to a stream which you are not aware of?
If it's a two-three months project, when you are preparing this project plan or the delivery approach, what is your approach? How is your approach to this whole project because we are not aware of the tech and the timeline is short.
What all do you cover while you get into these kinds of projects?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
In that case, say for example, if I don't know API, then I'll check within my team about the SMEs who are well versed with the SP technologies, and I'll connect with them and have a quick discussion with them and get more knowledge on it.
Like how it is, what it is, and how it can be built, what the prerequisites are for that, and what is required, all those things. I'll gather those details and then I'll connect with the appropriate stakeholder and get the information like what he's expecting from us, what kind of application, or what things he is looking into it.
I'll connect the lines of what I got the knowledge from the SME and what the client expectation is here. And if I'm missing anything from either side, like from the client or SME perspective, I'll get more information based on my questions there.
Once I connect all the dots, I'll prepare a plan like what is required, how many resources, and all those things. I'll prepare that and establish that...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
So for a two-month project, right? Assuming it's a two-month project that you are working on to prepare and layout and then work on the whole project. Category, so what all do you plan? What generally do you cover?
What are the critical data points or let's say milestones that you will look into to say that, "Hey, okay, this is a two-month project, and even a small slippage will run through into delayed delivery date."
So what exactly... Where will be your milestone approaches to say that the delivery as well as the project completion will be on track?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So for short-term projects, the major license... What I look here is about the requirements freeze and getting the technology, what to use, and dev team size, what team size is required, and how much experience
I have to look into it because based on the complexity of the project, I may have to look into senior resources here. If it's a normal web page or something like that, then I can utilize mid or lower-level experienced persons here.
But if it's a complex project, then definitely have to use senior resources. Even from the QER perspective and if it is required in the SQL-related, I'll put in the paper like all these as major milestones requirements and what is the text tack we are going to use, what is the dev milestone, what is the QA milestone, and what is the UT milestone?
If any UT users are there, then before the code comes into the QA, I'll ask them to involve in QA and U so that my timelines will not go beyond my committed lines. Because even if they step in at the time of the UT and if we see any major mismatch in the expected results, then we can have that particular time gap here if I involve them in the QA itself.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
So let's say a two-month project. I have to deliver five features inside. Let's say an Android application or iPhone application that you are building, right? Now in these two months, you have to complete development design, development UT, and go live, right?
So how will you break down the milestones or how will you plan this whole thing to complete in two weeks? We have five features to deliver and we have a total of eight weeks and then a complete UT and go live as well. Testing development. Go live UT...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Okay, two months. Since it's eight weeks, in the first week, I'll plan it all, like all the requirements gathering and finalizing the requirements and all. In the second week, I'll go ahead with the technology advice and what SQL or DE team... What their involvement is required and third, fourth, fifth, sixth, four weeks.
I'll fully dedicate that to their team, wherein they'll be... They have to implement all these features. Five stories or five features. In the seventh week, it would come to the QA and UT phases. At the end of the seventh week, even UT should be completed so that if any unexpected or major issues come at the early of the eighth week, those can be tested and fixed.
By the end of the eighth week, it will go for a live and all the users will be able to...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: This is...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: To use...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
The standard approach right that you are telling in. If you have to plan strategically, then how will you do it? Because whatever you mentioned is a pretty standard approach that we will look into.
But anything strategically that you can plan to make sure that we are aligned on the dates as well as even the features that we've made...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Technically, as in these five features, I'll check what are the complex areas and how much effort is required for this. Because even if it's some of the features, maybe a complex one, and it is dependent on...
I'll split this as a story BCDE and say, for example, if the story D is dependent on implementation of story A and C, which means story A and C should be completed first, then only I'll be able to complete story D here. Then, in that way, I'll put up my story or execution plan first, story A and C completed. Parallel story B and story E are independent. Then, I'll be
pushing that as well. Once story A and C are completed, or when we see they are yet to complete in the final stage, I'll ask our dev team and other team members to start implementing story D as well.
By the time story A and C are completed, story D will be started with 10 to 15% of completion. Once the story D is completed, and even story B and E are completed by the time... Once all these stories are completed, in the meantime, I'll ask the QA team to test the individual stories.
Once all these stories are completed, then I'll ask them to do integration and regression testing there so that by the time when all the stories are completed, we will be around a fifth or sixth week time, right?
Which means QA will not have sufficient time, and even the UT testing may not be possible if we see any major issues in QA. So, I'll minimize those QA issues by identifying them in QA itself. And when the QA and ut...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Apart from this project plan, what do you think will be the key role for a project manager or a scrum master while delivering these projects, right? What are the other things that you feel are important apart from this planning for a project manager to look into?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Time management cost costing because these all play a vital role in project management thing because if anyone is slipping either by timeline or a cost thing, then it will be a huge Sal will be there...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Other than this, there should be another factor which I feel is more important, like your visibility to the customer on the progress as well, right? Yeah. So that is a key factor that is part of project management.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
For two months' project, I mean what we do here is for two months' project we will have regular biweekly calls with them and we'll give this status update kind of thing. We have implemented these features and we are at this point of stage out of all the project plan, all those details, we will share those.
When it comes to the long-term project, right? So we will have a demo to the customer.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Even in the short term, I think we should include a demo. I know long term and short term. Long term there is a large scope of error. I mean, chance to do errors, but for short term, you...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yes.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
Don't have that opportunity. So that is where the criticality comes into play, right? Okay. While handling these multiple projects. So how would you kind of select your team size to say that? Okay. You are executing eight to nine projects, with a span of I think is like from eight to ten weeks, right?
So each of them might be in different stages. So how would you select your team to have these projects delivered? Because if you are owning those eight projects, how would you like your team composition to be?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So here's what I do. I'll be involved in PI planning and student planning as well, so that I'll get to know what features they are going to push in the upcoming release. So that's what happens here. I'll be able to understand what percentage of bandwidth is required by each team member.
Say, in a team, we will be having the QSL team and the data team. All these team members will be involved, right? So, for example, if in this upcoming feature, it's only 20 story points,
and already we have a three dev team there, which means I can be able to allocate only 50% of a QA there and data team if it is required. I'll allocate them. It depends on... I'll try to understand what is going to be implemented in that particular upcoming release.
Based on that, I'll have a discussion with the team members as well. How much bandwidth is required for all those things? Based on the size of the project as well. Overall, in some of the projects, out of these 22, almost six people are dedicated to that particular project.
Even I'll not be able to touch them for... I mean, I'm not able to take them for another project. So out of these 20-26 are dedicated for that long-term project. Even if any change request comes into the project...
Be able to have an allocation that's in my total hand.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
So coming to the other thing is again, I'll just give you a brief overview of how... I don't know if Raghu has already shared this or not, but for us, Devon QA is a single resource, okay? We... It's not a separate team because of these small-term projects, right? The whole development and testing team will be one guy, one team that will be doing it right, whether depending on the number of resources you plan to deliver and go on right.
So that is another key important role that we have to consider in the fact of execution. Okay. How will you successfully get to closure of a project? I know kickstarting a project is important. Likewise, a closure of a project is similarly important.
So what steps do you take before you call it off that this project is completed?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So first thing is I'll have a weekly or biweekly status call with the team members so that I'll get to know what the stage of the project implementation is. If I see any challenges faced by the team, then I'll go ahead with the appropriate action there.
If they are not finding any information or if they are not finding any right tool to implement, then based on the situation I'll try to resolve that issue. Once all these are done according to my plan, at the end of the project delivery, I'll ensure that this project is delivered based on what the client's requirement is there.
If he's expecting a beta call to see, then I'll ensure that I'll give a full demo to the client saying that this is what we have implemented and this is if you see here, this is the front-end backend. What? All the details, whatever it is required there.
I'll give a demo to them, and if there are any known issues, anything like that, then I'll let the client know that so that even he'll be on the same page and he may not be coming back to us. Like this is a bug or this is not expected like that. All those things will be discussed with him, and if he's expecting any other thing to be implemented, I take note of it.
If it is required, then we'll go ahead with the patch release. If not, we are good with that. I'll ensure him that if any maintenance work comes in the future, we will be taking a head based on the size of the work.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: So how will you plan to close or validate UI completion and go live completion and the next steps to closure? That was where my main question on closure of the project was. So yeah, I think... Yeah, go ahead. You're not saying anything more...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Yeah, if... As you mentioned, if a single person is doing everything like a dev, and all general perception is that if I'm developing something, I feel that whatever I implemented is correct,
and I may ignore some parts of testing here and there. There will definitely be a possibility of slippage to the production slip page to the production. If possible, I'll connect with the client and go through the application and see what he's expecting.
I'll give a proper demo of what he has expected based on the previous discussion. I'll bring those points and see whether those are implemented correctly or not in this phase itself. Once me and the client are satisfied with the product, then we'll go for the sign-off.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Because now you know, right? The whole approach is like the FD model where one does the whole thing right. So...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: No.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: The process needs to validate if everything is done or not. I know as a human whatever you mentioned is true that there is a chance of slippage, but I think the process or you are tracking from the project management perspective should cover to validate if we have completed everything or not. That's...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yes.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: My expectation. Do you think that is possible, or do you think that you can get that process implemented to validate or have confirmations that everything is done?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Mostly, we can do that by having some discussions and certain change process things, which we can go ahead with that based on what we are following right now and what tweaks we can do in our current process. Based on that, we can achieve that.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Okay, go. I think I am... Good. Go.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay, yeah. So a couple of questions from my side. So currently or in your previous projects, what are the KPIs you have as a project manager?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
As a project manager, I do have a timeline, is a first thing, and cost-effective. Beyond this, we have regular Scrum practice-related things. How many stories we are delivering and how much ROI or we are seeing out of it.
What is the sprint to sprint, how much percentage or how much valid deliverables we are seeing, and from the QA perspective, we will see what is the test effectiveness and the production bug slippage. All those things will have that.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay. So what are you involved in? Do you have a concept of SEASD, like your customers giving a customer satisfaction?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So we do have that, but not from the project perspective because the project is new, right? So CSAT will come only when the application is delivered and if any change requests are raised through service now, right?
So for those change requests, we will get that CSAT score. It's out of four, we should maintain at least more than 3.5. That is our target for all these things.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yeah. So how do you...

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: So how do you... So how do you make sure we are at a 3.5 out of four with all the customers? What are the few things you take care of so that we don't slip on our CSAT?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So there are a couple of things which we maintain here. First, it is about the time to react. For example, if I'm raising a CR right now. So how much time is it taking to react for that CR that will be assigned to one of the groups and the group team? They will pick that and see whether it's a config-related or a coaching-related issue. They'll do the price team... They will do the analysis, and if it is config-related or any other thing which they can do by themselves, they'll do it. Or if they see any data-related issue, they will approach the appropriate customer or the user who raised that here and let them know what I'm saying. This is recently what we have done. We have got to seize one customer's name. He implemented a module as well, and in his name as a customer's name, so that is throwing him an error.
So immediately he raised a CR, and if it's a data-related issue, then we will go ahead with that kind of resolution. If any of these things are not falling in, and still that is a required thing, then that will come as a change request to the dev team, and dev team will pick it up.
They will analyze whether this can be fixed within the sprint in the current sprint because that will be overhead activity at that point in time. They will pick that if it is feasible in that sprint, they will do the complete and QA complete, and all these things will be done.
Based on these things, we will let the customer or the user know that this is what we have done. Based on that, if it is a major feature which requires two weeks or three weeks of time, then because we have to let the user know that this will require this much of time to implement, based on that, they will give us a CR start score.
Because sometimes a user will be thinking that, "Okay, this is a short thing. Devim can do it in half a day. But while it is taking more than two weeks like that, the impression should not go to the user.
So we will properly communicate to the user like this is what happened with this year and we are going to implement this in the upcoming split and the beta for this to complete is this data and as submitted.
If you are not able to do that as for the committed timelines, then our CSP score will go down and there are a lot of many parameters which are involved while calculating this CSP score, like time to react and whether the issue has been resolved within the given timeline or not, and whether all the users, I mean their team, are approachable or not.
Because sometimes these CS come from Mexico and other team members as well. They are not directly connected with us. So we insurers will properly communicate.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: A common...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: This will take this much of...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Was. Differentend...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Time and all those things will be communicated properly. So that even that user will understand. Okay, they have given this timeline and they'll be doing it understood.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay, so quality of delivery is one key area, right? Delivering on time is one key area, but the quality of code, what we are delivering, is another key area. So in our whole SDLC life cycle, what do you think is the major area which will improve the quality of delivery?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
The first thing is about the requirements gathering because if the requirement is not correct and if you change the requirement frequently, even the dev team, QA team, and entire team will suffer a lot with those things.
So we have to connect with the appropriate stakeholders here and gather the requirements properly and get a proper sign from them. It's not that what I understand, it's about what I understand is the what you understand. We both are on the same page.
That is what we have to see, and that is the main reason why we do this here. When we get the requirements right, we will draw down into the epic features stories, and when the story comes into the picture, even the title and the description of the story, the acceptance criteria, and the other details like whether the negative or positive scenarios are to be implemented or not. All those proper details will be covered in that particular story so that whenever that story is picked by the dev team or a QA team, they will go through the story and understand it and analyze it, and then they'll start the implementation.
If, in case they have any questions, they will reach out to us. Otherwise, they will implement that and complete that. As for the story acceptance criteria here, as I mentioned right, if the requirements are clear, then the next phases will be easier.
The dev team, the QA team, and of course, the dev team, whatever they implement, we need to check. QA has to check whether they have implemented right or not. Not that comes into the testing phase.
But the first step is about the requirements thing, because if the requirements are not clear, then it will be tough for us to identify whether we are going good or not. Yeah, so the requirements.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Everything is clear, but still, where it can fail... Everything is clear, the requirements are signed off, but still, where we can go wrong with the quality of the dev team's understanding.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Because as I mentioned, right, so, I can say this if the even though the line says implement a login page. Okay, so the dev team might be understanding in a different way. Because if I'm seeing a login page, it can have a username password, and the username can be a minimum of 8 to 20 characters, or it can be an email ID, or it can be a mobile number.
So all these things to be documented in that particular story, and in the sprint planning, we have to let the dev team know what we have to implement. And in that way, we will be removing that gap between the requirements and the understanding here that we will catch the...

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Those are gaps how we will catch it like.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Whatever gaps are here. In some cases, we can have a reverse KY kind of thing wherein what I told... Can you repeat that so that once you repeat it, if I'm satisfied with that, which means we are both on the same page,
otherwise, if you got stuck in some point of line, then, okay, you may not have understood. What are the requirements here? Then we will go over the requirements analysis again and check. This is what we have to implement as for the requirements.
Similarly, the same should happen between the QAs as well, because if QER doesn't understand the requirements properly, they'll not be able to test it thoroughly. If they don't test it thoroughly, obviously there will be a production bug.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So the first thing is about the communication and collaboration should be stronger between the teams so that whatever the requirements are there, it has been understood by each and every team member and if they have any questions, they have to come up immediately.
It's not at the last stage of the deliverables they have to come right? Time is important here, so... Okay, frequent connections, frequent collaboration is required to implement in the right way.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Okay, so like so testing will play a bigger role, right in the quality of delivery. So to say, I see a lot of developers, like, they are passionate about developing and all, but like, when it comes to testing, a lot of people like, get relaxed or like, they don't take testing seriously.
So how will you make sure like a testing is done thoroughly? Like what is the process you enforce?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So we have defined the process here. When it comes into the dev, because even in dev them sometimes what I used to do was some code reviews here. So what they used to do is they'd write the code line by line, but they wouldn't put any comments.
So in that case, what happens here is if whatever the quote I have written here, if you are going to review it, you will not understand it. So in the future, when the story or something comes to your bucket,
if you are reviewing my code, you'll not be able to identify where you have to fix it. So we will ensure that all the industry standards...
Advise the team. They have to analyze it properly, and they have to write the test cases, prepare the test dataset, and ensure that all the scenarios have been covered by having the traceability matrix document.
They have to map whether the requirements and tests are covering 100% or not. Test coverage is one of the important factors here. If they find any bugs, they should be communicated via SS management tool itself, like a bug in the system, not through an email or some team set or something like that.
Because... I'm saying this is because sometimes what happens... I raised a bug today, and I have communicated through verbal or through teams, and Dave has fixed it. But somehow that fix hasn't gone to the production, which means that bug is again occurring in the production environment.
So at that point of time, if a user is seeing that, the first question that comes to their mind is, "Why it is not implemented or why it is not tested?" So what I see thoroughly is that regularly you have to document each and everything like a test case, a screenshot for reporting, and if you are finding any bug, you put all the details why, where, and how. All those details should be incorporated in those bug details so that even if a layman is seeing that particular bug, he should be able to reproduce it with the same version. They have to mention the version number as well. In some cases, this bug may occur in lower versions,
but not in the next version. I'll that this process is implemented and thoroughly followed because in most cases, what happens is we will define the process, but due to some timeline things, we will not follow it.
So, in that case, I'll give some exceptions in some of the cases because if tomorrow is release, I cannot go and ask my team member to write a test case now because it will take us time and it will impact the project delivery.
So, at least okay, you test it today. You gather all the screenshots roughly in your system, and once the deliverable is completed, then you document it so that, as and when you require in the next phases, it will be easy for you to look into what you have tested, what the screenshots you have, how you tested, what data you used, all those things you can see.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Got it. Yeah, I think I'm a good...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: One last question so I...

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Yes. TA.

content.text: Do you know all of your project deliveries till now? How is it? How was the team placed around in one geo location in office in remote? How was the delivery happening? And do you think your approach to the project management would change depending upon this placement? Or does it not care much about where the resource is?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: No, it doesn't depend because my resources are located in Hyderabad, who sits next to me. Some resources are in Bangalore, and some are in the US and Mexico as well.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Got it. Okay, I think...

content.text: For all these three, we have AI, different time zones even. We have only one common day, which is Thursday, between Bangalore and Hyderabad. Because we go to office on Thursday and Friday, and the Bangalore team will come to office on Wednesday and Thursday.

content.text: Okay...

You know how the traffic will be. So I'll look into those external factors as well while communicating with them.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Got it. How is your inclusion towards AI in the whole process of delivery? Have you been doing something or you have...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yes...

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Been adopting...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
I was discussing with Raghu last time. So we have an approved AI tool which is full-side AI because as for the company standard policy, we should not use external AI like Claude, ChatGPT, and all.
So this guy has agreed to install on our servers.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Love? Nothing like it.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: So all these LLMs and LLaMA, which is currently 5.0 right now. Earlier it was 4.5. So this has been deployed into our system and we are utilizing that for core generation and test case and test automation generation here.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Nice afternoon. Okay? Yep, okay, I think I'm good. It was nice talking to you.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Same here.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Thank you, thanks for reading, thank you.
